minutes_text:
INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

The Arts Commission meeting was held on Wednesday, May 15, 2019 in Community Room A located on the first
floor of City Hall. Commissioner Althea Metcalf called the meeting to order at 6:30 p.m. followed by the flag salute.

Roll Call

  Present
  Commissioner Althea Metcalf, District 1
  Commissioner Phyllis Battle, District 3
  Commissioner Vicki Perryman-Banks, District 4
  Sabrina Barnes, Director Parks, Recreation and Community Services Department
  Helen Lessick, Public Art Consultant
  Stephanie Maldonado, Senior Management Assistant
  Absent
  None

  Sabrina Barnes informed the Commission that Commissioner Fox has resigned. The Commission is awaiting
appointment of new Commissioners from Mayor James Butts and Councilman Padilla.

Approval of the Minutes

  There was a correction on the March 20, 2019 minutes, revising the amount of the action item; from $36,300
to $130,256. The minutes were then moved by Commissioner Banks and seconded by Commissioner Battle.

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Banks and Battle
  Nays: None
Staff Report

  Director Barnes presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission receive and file the IGAPP
2019 Music Composition and Performance panel recommendations for each semi-finalist to submit a new two-
minute audio sketch showing the direction each would take and give the Commission opportunity with a written
narrative about the performance. Helen Lessick provided information regarding the panel. The panel was held on
April 11, 2019. It’s a commission for $12,000 for music composition and performance. The applications were
received through the end of May. Two semi-finalists were recommended. Commissioner Battle was on the panel
and stated that the experience was memorable and the candidates that were chosen were well deserved. The semi-
finalists are Jabari Lake and Dr. Dawn Norfleet and Kevin Deane (team). They are Inglewood artist; both own
businesses in Inglewood. The Commission was advised to review their resumes. Commissioner Battle inquired if
the information presented was based on rank. Ms. Lessick stated that they are not ranked. Each of the semi-finalists
will be paid $1,000 to create a sketch and narrative of how they will proceed. . They have 8-weeks to develop their
sketch. The panel will reconvene in July where a finalist will be chosen. Ms. Barnes stated the panel was passionate
about their choices and that there was a general consensus on who the semi-finalist were. Commissioner Metcalf
inquired on the number of applicants. There were six (6) applicants total.

  1
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

  Director Barnes presented a staff report recommending the Arts Commission recommend the Mayor and
Council Members accession Cosmic Fusion, the public art mural by Ricardo Duffy into the City of Inglewood Public
Art Collection, making it eligible for maintenance and conservation through Public Art Fund allocations. Helen Lessick
provided information regarding the mural. Cosmic Fusion is an addition to Culture Fusion. The piece was a
Successor Agency project (former Redevelopment Agency). Cosmic Fusion is adjacent to the Public Art Piece
Culture Fusion and is recommended that it is added to the Public Art collection; in the future a conservator will treat
both murals equally. Cosmic Fusion is a ceramic tile mural that should last for 50 years. Commissioner Banks made
a motion that the Arts Commission recommend the Mayor and Council Members accession Cosmic Fusion, the
public art mural by Ricardo Duffy, into the City of Inglewood Public Art Collection, making it eligible for maintenance
and conservation through Public Art Fund allocations. Commissioner Metcalf seconded and the motion was
approved as follows:

  Ayes: Commissioners Metcalf, Battle and Banks
  Nayes: None

Verbal Reports

IGAPP 2020: Participator Public Art for Dr. Martin Luther King Day

  IGAPP 2020 will include the values and spirit of Dr. King. Artists are to propose ideas for the
commemoration. Twenty artists have been identified for the call. Sixty percent (60%) of those artists that responded
are from Inglewood. Arts presenters are being invited to present proposals and are as follows: Aero Collective,
Creative House, Residency, and Sip and Sonder. The funding for this project was allocated in 2018-2019. The
piece must be completed by January 18, 2020. Ms Lessick stated that the panel needs to move fairly quickly
because of the time frame allotted for completion. The contract will be for creative services; various forms of art. It
will be a standard City of Inglewood contract that includes general liability insurance as well as a current business
license. Commissioner Battle asked if the Commission could add a provision in the contract to assist with insurance
and licensing fees. Sabrina Barnes stated that the City of Inglewood has a general policy that contractor must be
insured to do work with the City. Helen Lessick stated that in the past a non-profit has stepped forward and
sponsored the artist. Commissioner Banks asked if assisting the artist could possible enable them. Ms. Barnes
stated that the Department is looking into a blanket policy that could serve as a “catch all” but at this time all artists
are responsible for their own insurance.

Public Comments

  Helen Lessick stated that the Public Art Coalition of Southern California had a meeting last month at Metro.
Two booklets were developed and given to Sabrina Barnes.

Commissioners’ Comments

  None

  2
   INGLEWOOD  CALIFORNIA

  ARTS COMMISSION

Announcements/ Calendar

  The next Art Commission meeting will be held at the City of Inglewood in Community Room A on June 19,
2019 at 6:30 p.m.

  With no further business, the meeting was adjourned at 6:59 p.m.
